references.text: Jesus answers the apostles' prayer for more faith by explaining that even faith as small as a mustard seed can accomplish great things ([ref:Luk 17:6|Luke 17:6]).
A father cries out with a similar prayer: "I believe; help my unbelief!" This expresses the same need for the Lord to strengthen faith ([ref:Mark 9:24|Mark 9:24]).
Jesus teaches the disciples that faith like a mustard seed can move mountains, which parallels his response to the apostles' prayer for increased faith ([ref:Matt 17:20|Matthew 17:20]).
Paul describes faith as something God works and brings to completion, just as the apostles here ask the Lord to give them more faith – faith is a gift from God ([ref:Fil 1:25|Philippians 1:25]).
Paul emphasizes that faith is a gift from God, not something people produce on their own. This aligns with the apostles' prayer to the Lord to increase their faith ([ref:Ef 2:8-9|Ephesians 2:8-9]).
Jesus is called "the author and perfecter of faith," confirming that faith originates in him – therefore it is right to ask him to increase it ([ref:Hebr 12:2|Hebrews 12:2]).
Jesus prays for Peter that his faith may not fail, showing that the preservation and strength of faith depend on the Lord's help ([ref:Luk 22:32|Luke 22:32]).
The parable of the mustard seed illustrates how something very small can grow into something large, an image Jesus also uses to describe the power of faith ([ref:Matt 13:31-32|Matthew 13:31-32]).

Paul mentions faith as one of the gifts of the Spirit, emphasizing that faith is something God gives, in line with the apostles' prayer for the Lord to give them more faith ([ref:1 Kor 12:9|1 Corinthians 12:9]).
